critical_code_review_comments: server.py:730 The action-label heuristic labels a PUT as 'published' ONLY when the request body contains EXACTLY {'published': true} and nothing else. But the frontend PostEditor (BlogTab.jsx:157) always sends the ENTIRE draft on edit (title, body, excerpt, cover, category, date, readMinutes, published…). Consequence: toggling publish from the admin UI's edit drawer produces an 'updated' audit row, not 'published'. The observed changed_fields for a UI toggle was ['body','category','cover','date','excerpt','published','readMinutes','title']. If the intent is that a user-visible 'toggle publish' UX shows up as PUBLISHED in history, either (a) add a dedicated publish/unpublish toggle in BlogTab.jsx that PATCHes only {published: bool}, or (b) broaden the backend heuristic to label it 'published' whenever the payload's `published` value flipped versus the current DB doc (regardless of other fields). Confirmed working when the caller sends published-only (e.g. via API/scripting), which is why the pytest suite passes.

server.py:757 admin_blog_audit uses `min(max(limit, 1), 500)` — this silently coerces `limit=0` to 1 and `limit=-5` to 1 rather than rejecting them with 422. Not a bug (defensive), but a Query(gt=0, le=500) would surface bad input to callers.

server.py:748-757 The endpoint has no pagination cursor (offset/skip). For long-lived deployments the last 500 rows are all that's inspectable — earlier history is unreachable via API. Consider adding `?before=<iso_ts>` for backfill browsing in a follow-up.

server.py:703 _log_audit swallows all exceptions with a warning. Correct choice (never break CRUD if audit write fails), but there's no retry/dead-letter — if Mongo is unhealthy audit rows are permanently missing. Consider a small in-memory buffer + retry-on-next-request, or at minimum emit a Prometheus counter so ops can alarm on `audit_write_failures_total`.

server.py:689 `_actor_from_session` returns the literal string 'unknown' when session.token is missing/empty. Because require_admin already guarantees a valid session dict is present, this branch should never fire in production — but if it ever does, the drawer will show 'by unknown' with no way to distinguish machine actors. Consider raising/logging instead.

BlogTab.jsx:519-535 HistoryDrawer's useEffect fetches ONCE on mount and never on re-open (because the component unmounts on close). Correct as-is, but note: if the drawer is open while a background CRUD happens elsewhere, the list is stale. A small [Refresh] button inside the drawer would help — cheap addition.

BlogTab.jsx:576 `key={r.id}` is fine (each audit row has a UUID), but the row's data-testid `blog-history-row-${r.id}` uses the UUID — main agent scripts probably won't be able to target a specific row by index/slug/action. Consider adding a secondary data-testid like `data-testid-slug={r.slug}` or `data-action={r.action}` on each `<li>` so testing agents can query 'give me the newest CREATED row for slug X' without parsing text content.

Backend heuristic: PUT with body === {published: <bool>} logs 'published'/'unpublished'; ANY other combination (even {published:true, title:'x'}) logs 'updated' — the frontend's PostEditor sends all fields so its publish-toggle produces 'updated' rows, not 'published'. Endpoint accepts ?slug=<x>&limit=<n> (default 100, hard-cap 500, min 1).
rca of the issue: First-run failure of test_different_sessions_produce_different_actor_hashes: the scratch slugs contained uppercase 'A'/'B' ('pytest-audit-A-…'), which the backend's BlogPostBase Pydantic validator rejects with 422 (slug regex is `^[a-z0-9-]+$`). Because the POST failed silently in the test setup, the subsequent audit query returned an empty list. Fix: lowercase the discriminator ('sa'/'sb'). All 9 audit tests pass after the fix.
